chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you do not know whether you have prayed two or four, and your doubt does not lean towards anything specific, then perform the Tashahhud and offer the Salām, then pray two Rak'at and four Sajdahs, reciting Umm al-Qur'an in both of them, then perform the Tashahhud and offer the Salām. So if you had only prayed two, these two would complete the four, and if you had prayed four, these two would be optional (Nafl).

And if you do not know whether you have prayed three or four, and your doubt does not lean towards anything specific, then offer the Salām, then pray two Rak'at while you are seated, reciting in them Umm al-Kitab. And if your doubt leans towards the three, then stand and pray the fourth Rak'ah and do not perform the two Sajdahs of forgetfulness. So if your doubt leans towards the four, then perform the Tashahhud and offer the Salām, then perform the two Sajdahs of forgetfulness.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for completing prayer when unsure if you prayed two, three, or four Rak'at?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the jurisprudential methodology for resolving uncertainty (Shakk) in obligatory prayers, distinguishing between neutral doubt and doubt leaning towards a specific number. It establishes the principle of 'building on certainty' (Al-Istishab) by prescribing distinct corrective actions, such as completing the prayer or performing Sajdah al-Sahw, to ensure validity without excessive burden. This reflects the Shia emphasis on practical ease (Taysir) while maintaining ritual precision in daily worship.
